stories.title: FCC approves SpaceX plan to put AI data centers in space
stories.take: The FCC waved through SpaceX's plan for orbital AI data centers, ruling opponents' science concerns outside its authority — the space-compute era just got its permit.

stories.title: OpenAI says heavy ChatGPT users may hit limits sooner as it merges Chat and Work
stories.take: OpenAI is merging Chat and Work into one ChatGPT experience with a single usage meter — and heavy users may hit their limits sooner.

stories.title: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei calls accusations of surrendering human control to AI ‘absurd’
stories.take: Anthropic's Dario Amodei calls claims he's surrendering human control to AI 'absurd,' even as the labs automate more of their own research.

stories.title: 1Password said hackers broke into its internal systems, but customer passwords are safe
stories.take: Hackers broke into a 1Password employee's corporate account and took some customer information — the company says customer passwords themselves are safe.

stories.title: Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs
stories.take: State AGs are fighting Character.AI's bankruptcy plan to auction private chats, which cover 21 million U.S. accounts including 2.1 million minors.

stories.title: How data centers are driving a US natural-gas boom
stories.take: AI's power hunger is driving a U.S. natural-gas boom — the buildout is locking in gas plants faster than renewables can fill the gap.

stories.title: Brandweek 2026: Consumer-First Still Beats AI-First ft. Laura Knebusch
stories.take: Brandweek's takeaway, via GE's Laura Knebusch: 100 data sources, one source of truth — consumer-first still beats AI-first.

stories.title: Target’s New AI Assistant Is Just For Browsing, For Now
stories.take: Target's new 'Ask Target' AI assistant can browse with you, but it can't order or touch your account yet — commerce stays human for now.

stories.title: How Hershey strategized its brand film to be more than a 90-minute ad

stories.title: How YouTube, LEGO, Pokémon, and McDonald's are winning with Gen Alpha
stories.take: YouTube, LEGO, Pokémon and McDonald's are winning Gen Alpha by baking what kids say they want — and how they want to feel — into the core brand experience.

stories.take: CBA talks: league and MLBPA traded new revenue-sharing proposals as the Dec. 1 deadline nears and a work stoppage looms.

stories.title: Inflation remains stubbornly high, despite a drop in gas prices
stories.take: Inflation stays stubborn: consumer prices rose 3.8% in October from a year earlier, up from 3.6% in September, even as gas prices fell.

stories.title: What to talk about this Thanksgiving (other than politics)
stories.take: Talk about this instead: the royal family — Meghan and Harry back in the UK, William's slimmed-down monarchy • The new James Bond — Pattinson in, Josh O'Connor walked away from the fame • If politics lands anyway, common ground exists: nobody wants a data center in their backyard, and everyone feels the affordability squeeze • Deflection kit from three political reporters: pivot to a personal question, ask what's behind the anger, or go content-free with 'Can you believe it?'

stories.title: US Targets China, EU With New Tariffs Citing Overcapacity
stories.take: New tariffs target 'excess capacity,' with China hit hardest and findings tailored for 14 of 16 countries • Rates: Japan, Korea, Switzerland and the EU at 15%, possibly 20% — and NOT stacked on the summer levies • Dell check-in: AI demand intact (25% AI-server CAGR through 2029) but investors are selling the valuation anyway • Democrats plan to open January by attacking the Canada tariffs first; effective global tariff rate heading back to ~17%

stories.title: Inheritance Now
stories.take: Boomers hold ~$90 trillion — and their kids are asking why help has to wait for a funeral • One listener's dad dangles $250K while balking at $700K starter homes • 'Die With Zero' author Bill Perkins: money does the most good at 28–33, so give it while you're alive to see it • The boomer counter: early money robs kids of self-reliance — the fix both sides land on is actually talking about the numbers
